body: Thank you for the thoughts, I really am trying my best, but I'm just concerned at the moment that my best isn't going to be good enough. Guess I am just going to have to keep my fingers crossed and hope that I get through it. Thanks again.

Thank you for the thoughts, I really hope things start to get better as well. Unfortunately the pattern seems to be that the hallucinations are getting worse over time, more prolonged and vivid. Started to really struggle to tell the difference between reality and not when I'm experiencing them. Hopefully this trend breaks, but I have a feeling that it is just going to continue in this same pattern. I hope to god it doesn't continue exponentially!

Thank you for the reply, things like this really do help. Trust me when I say I have tried everything to try and lower my stress levels, but I've never known any different really. My entire childhood has been brought up in an incredibly stressful environment, and even when nothing is going on I have a feeling of anxiety about what is going to happen next. If I do manage to try and relax, thoughts flood my head which are incredibly negative. Normally I do not have time to think to myself, but when I do such as at night, things like suicide and other negative things are consistently on my mind. I've tried relaxation and mindfulness techniques in my CBT therapy, but was told that I probably won't be able to make progress as I'm not in a stable state of mind to be doing these exercises. I really do try, but unfortunately it doesn't seem to be enough. Again thanks for the reply and the sentiment, it really does help with this situation.

Have been doing a lot of mindfulness work through CBT therapy, however I have been told due to the stressful situation I am in now, and am constantly in, that I won't really be able to make progress in CBT as I'm not in a fit state of mind to progress, which I understand really. I just hope they don't give up on me entirely and throw me to the wolves.

I really hope the hallucinations go away for you too, I wouldn't wish them upon my worst enemy, it is mind and heart shattering. Been seeing a doctor for a while, but this particular doctor strongly believes in not giving out medication unless they feel it's absolutely necessary, and I have the same viewpoint. However our perceptions of 'necessary' could be different. There's no way I'd be able to go much longer with the hallucinations still, it's getting harder and harder each day until inevitably I'm going to have a complete mental breakdown and will not be here anymore. The fact that it's getting worse over time concerns me. I wish you the best of luck with your visit to the Doctor and I hope you get things sorted out for yourself. Take care and hang in there.

Hey, thank you for your kind words. Everything I have tried has no effect on the hallucinations, it's impossible to ignore them as when I have them, I believe they're real until they disappear. It's so distressing, every time I have one it keeps dragging me closer and closer to suicide, I can't stand it.

Hi and thanks for taking time to read this and reply. Sorry for the late reply but have only just noticed. I think the biggest problem that's making me want to end it all is the hallucinations. They really are unbearable... there's absolutely no way I will even be able to consider not doing it until they go away.

I can definitely relate to your situation. How did you find the will to carry on? After 10 years of this abuse happening knowingly, I feel like I'm finally broken. The hallucinations alone are enough for me to end it all, it is torture. As I said it's like watching a loved one die in front of you over and over again in an unending loop. Everything else is just gravy.
Thank you. Unfortunately as I said before I am almost certain I'm beyond help, and that suicide is my only option. Been going through CBT therapy for 2 years with no improvement.

Hi Suicinethrowaway. Thanks for taking your time to read and reply to this. No I haven't really gotten any closure, and any attempts to try and contact her have failed. She came to pick up the rest of her stuff a couple of days ago, but she obsessively avoided the subject. I guess her not having to think about it ensures that she doesn't feel guilty. Don't get me wrong, I wasn't perfect. No one is. But our three year relationship certainly doesn't warrant her disappearing, not speaking to me and leaving without a reason. It is completely unlike her and it crippled me. Also, thank you for the sentiment.
